scope: Verifier-only main-page readiness repair. The exact published helper and tests passed isolated real Windows unit checks and full TypeScript checking. These checks do not execute or admit an installed application, native Save dialog or retained-memory lifecycle.

priorInstalledFailure.observedFailure: The 30-second expected-origin page predicate at launchInstalled line 296 returned false until timeout. It follows the CDP connection and executable/nonce checks in the tested source, but no completed launch was serialized.

sourceBudgetMismatch.ordering: Production startup awaits startBackend before mainWindow. The former verifier page poll allowed only 30 seconds after CDP ownership admission, so it could end while the existing backend allowance remained valid.
sourceBudgetMismatch.inferenceLimit: This establishes an incorrect verifier bound. It is not a measured explanation of the missing page in the original run.

preservation.wholeOriginalSourceReconstruction: Removing the new helper and replacing the extracted launch block with its previous bytes reconstructs the full original verifier exactly.
preservation.existingTests: All 19 prior tests retain their exact source bytes except the import addition of vi. Seven new readiness tests are appended.
preservation.redToGreen: Within the verifier source, only the helper's 30000 constant changes to 80000, with a two-line comment explaining the existing 60-second backend plus 20-second native surface envelope. The test blob is identical. The separate green workflow also expands the selected-test command to both custody/native Save helper suites and adds full typecheck.

repair.scope: Only expected-origin application-page discovery inside the installed verifier.
repair.ownerRevalidation: The same Browser.getBrowserCommandLine executable and nonce assertions are extracted into one callback. A candidate is revalidated after awaiting that callback. A rejected ownership check fails without retry.
repair.processLiveness: Spawned-child exit, signal or launch failure is checked on discovery iterations and a 250-millisecond guard that remains active during an awaited ownership recheck. The guard rejects without waiting for the full deadline.
repair.candidateAdmission: Candidate must be open, have exactly the expected loopback origin, have no URL credentials, remain the same object in the current browser page list, and retain that origin after owner revalidation.
repair.lateCompletion: One whole-operation deadline covers waiting and pending owner revalidation. Settlement clears timers; a late owner completion cannot emit new observations or return a page.
repair.cleanup: Existing cleanup statements are unchanged. Revalidation clears the verifiedOwner claim before checking again; a failed claim cannot authorize browser-close adoption. The originally spawned child remains the only process-tree termination target.

fixtureObservationCountAssertion.basis: The fake-clock fixture with a stable missing page asserts at most eight observations. This is not an explicit runtime array-length cap.

diagnostics.runtimeBound: The helper has an 80000-ms operation deadline, 15000-ms waiting checkpoints and fixed metadata fields. Candidate revalidation may emit additional observations; no hard eight-entry cap is implemented.
